dossier.public_summary: The 13.4-day dip on this M dwarf appears only in two deep single-sector events and disappears in others, with transit depths ranging from ~27,000 ppm to negative values. The light-curve source itself varies by a factor of >260 between sectors and the star shows large astrometric noise (RUWE 11.72) and strong 7-day spot variability. Together this favours a few spurious dips or blended variability over a steady transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by hundreds of percent between sectors (12721 ppm to -1127 ppm) - alone not a reject criterion per rules, but confirms variation is real, not calibration.

Hole is confirmed by single light-curve source (QLP) p_constant_all 2.020851281189415e-40. So sector-to-sector change is not a calibration difference between products; it is real in the same aperture and pipeline.

Individual transits are inconsistent (chi2 209.06 dof 6). Share_of_top_3 0.986 shows the signal is carried by two deep events: 27519 ppm (8.2 sigma) and 20699 ppm (7.2 sigma), while five other events are at 2083 ppm, -1326 ppm etc. This is a few bad transits driving the period, not a steady planet.
4 transits near gaps out of 7 with expected_share 0.2228 is unlikely, supporting that dips are not consistently recovered; non-detections (sectors 58, 86 depth ~2533 ppm and -1127 ppm) match this.

Large astrometric excess noise indicates the target is itself a binary/evolved star. Phase curve swing (ratio_to_depth 0.04242) and strong 7.159 d rotation at 40-11000 ppm variability provide alternative astrophysical variability, favouring spot / binary systematics over a planet.

reasons.why: Flat-bottom, no odd/even or secondary on target and duration ratio 0.84 do not positively favour a planet and do not outweigh the positive evidence for variability / few-event signal. Neutrals are outweighed by strong depth-inconsistency and ruwe.
